chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What is the ruling for a man who makes a solemn oath (ila') from his wife before he has intercourse with her?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The solemn oath does not take effect until he has intercourse with her.'

key_terms.إِيلَاءُ: Solemn oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: He enters into her (consummation of marriage/intercourse)

ai.seo_question: When does the solemn oath of abstention (Ila') take effect in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a key juristic condition for 'ila' (solemn oath of abstention), establishing that the oath only becomes legally binding after consummation (dakhul), thereby distinguishing it from pre-consummation vows. This ruling ensures that the four-month waiting period for divorce, as prescribed in the Quran, applies specifically to cases where conjugal rights have already been established, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise legal causality in marital disputes.
